commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[deps] Require ShellSim 0.1.20 (#9477)

Raise the marin-core ShellSim requirement from 0.1.10 to 0.1.20 and the
shellbox `shellsim` extra from 0.1.17 to 0.1.20, and lock 0.1.20.

The new releases run WebAssembly executables as scheduled processes, add
PIPESTATUS, a boot-time real-time clock mode, native complex numbers and
NumPy complex128 arrays, and give shells exec'd from pipelines their own
`$$`. The Python `Environment` API used by the Chat workspaces and the
shellbox backend only gained additions since 0.1.10.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[eval] Register the checked-in publication-policy benchmark configs (#9476)

MMLU-Pro, GPQA Diamond, CRUXEval, FinanceBench, IFEval, IFBench and MRCR
have checked-in Evalchemy configs under
`experiments/evaluation/configs/evalchemy/`, but no entry in `EVALS`.
Only `--evalchemy-config` could launch them, and experiment code that
calls `eval_step`, which resolves names through `EVALS`, failed with
"unknown eval(s)" at run time.

The configs are registered by name. They remain outside every suite, so
the `chat` suite and the other named selections are unchanged.
FinanceBench's judge block comes from its config file, as it does for
`--evalchemy-config`.

---

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[iris] Give Docker setup at least one CPU (#9474)

Give Docker setup containers the larger of one CPU and the task's CPU
request. The run container keeps the task's requested allocation.
Reserved and preemptible workers enforce a quota; on-demand workers use
relative CPU shares.

A task requesting 0.1 CPU previously ran dependency builds under a
0.1-core quota on reserved workers. A [recent
job](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fpower%2Fcurriculum-math-generate-20260926?user=power)
spent 1m47s preparing 19 packages, including 16 workspace builds. The
setup floor lets those transient builds use up to one core. Concurrent
setups can temporarily consume more CPU than their scheduler
reservations.

---------

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[levanter] Keep HF export shard writers out of multi-host collectives (#9473)

Concurrent HF export (#9471) runs shard writers in a thread pool on
process 0
only, but two calls inside the writer entered multi-host collectives:
haliax `save_state_dict` and `upload_to_hub` both end in
`sync_global_devices`, a `psum`. Process 0 entered the collective from a
worker
thread while the other hosts moved on to the next shard's all-gather, so
any
multi-host export diverged. Under the Iris GPU compile guard it failed
with
`GPU compile fingerprint mismatch` (process 0 compiled `_psum` where the
others
compiled `_to_state_dict_with_dtype`); without the guard it would hang.

Shard writers now call `safetensors.numpy.save_file` directly, and Hub
uploads
from `save_pretrained` go through a process-0 helper that has no
barrier.
`upload_to_hub` keeps its barrier for its other callers. For
object-store
destinations, `temp_dir_before_upload` still synchronizes all processes
after
the metadata upload.

---------

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[levanter] Export HF checkpoint shards concurrently (#9471)

Export Hugging Face checkpoint shards through concurrent writers on
process 0. Every process gathers tensor values in the same shard and
parameter order, keeping multi-host collectives matched. A 16 GiB host
budget reserves twice each shard's payload until serialization and
upload finish; a shard larger than the target runs alone. Metadata is
written after all shard uploads complete. The export command exposes the
budget and writer count.

A four-device CPU benchmark exported eight shards and 829,193 bytes with
an 80 ms simulated upload delay per shard. One writer took 0.949
seconds; four writers took 0.254 seconds. This measures local latency
overlap, not the 67B multi-node export.

---------
